text:
nina: noticed S3 upload from partner with file `partner-a/keys/wrapped_ssh_key.b64` that looks like a KMS-wrapped blob. path: `s3://partner-ingest-prod/ingest/2026/02/12/wrapped_ssh_key.b64`. tagging you all because it contains `kms_key: projects/partner-prod/locations/global/keyRings/kr/cryptoKeys/ssh-wrap`

rashid: can you paste the object metadata? any headers showing origin or intent?

nina: metadata snippet redacted:
```
{"x-amz-meta-origin":"partner-ci","x-amz-meta-type":"wrapped-ssh","kms-key":"projects/partner-prod/.../cryptoKeys/ssh-wrap","etag":"abc123"}
```

ops-runner: Created alert: ALERT-2026-1916 1: S3 object with external KMS key detected in ingest bucket.

tara: Quick risk call: do we accept wrapped SSH keys? our policy only allows wrapped creds if they use our KMS or an approved cross-project grant. This looks partner-owned.

maria: Agreed. Immediate actions: 1) Quarantine object (move to locked bucket) 2) Audit any Vault entries referencing this object 3) Notify partner and ask them to stop sending until we have a protocol 4) Start rotation plan for any secrets that could be tied to it.

nina: quarantined to `s3://sec-quarantine/INC-2026-1916/partner-a/wrapped_ssh_key.b64` and set deny-lifecycle so it isn't auto-deleted. Put ACL to private.

rashid: Search underway for other occurrences. Running:
```
aws s3api list-objects --bucket partner-ingest-prod --query "Contents[?contains(Key,'wrapped')].Key"
```
I'll post results.

ops-runner: Audit hint: we found 3 other files matching `wrapped_*ssh*` across last 72h. Uploading list to the incident.

tara: Important: if service expects plaintext SSH key, someone might have a consumer that attempts to decrypt. Check for decrypt attempts in KMS and Vault logs.

maria: Good point. Check Cloud KMS logs for `Decrypt` calls where principal belongs to our project. Also check Vault audit for `transit/decrypt` or `sys/unwrap`.

rashid: quick KMS query I ran (redacted): 0 Decrypt API calls with ciphertext matching that blob. So far no consumption.

nina: Who onboarded this partner? there should be a checklist requiring specifying key principals.

tara: Onboarding owner is @maria, flagged for follow-up. We need to add a required step: ensure partner KMS keys are either whitelisted or they provide signed attestations and rotate windows.

maria: I'll take onboarding action item. Also we need RBAC change: remove any broad `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` grants to member `serviceAccount:partner-ingest@partner-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` in our project. Only allow rewrap bridges if they use a pre-agreed key. Drafting IAM delta now.

ops-runner: Note on audit forwarding: ensure Cloud KMS admin log category and Data Access logs for `Encrypt`/`Decrypt` are exported to SIEM for the last 90d. Add filter: `protoPayload.serviceName="cloudkms.googleapis.com" && protoPayload.methodName:("Encrypt" OR "Decrypt")`

nina: For remediation we should: 1) rotate any SSH keys we issued to partner in last 90d, 2) mark the quarantined object as TTL 30d pending partner proof of origin, 3) add validation on ingestion to reject external-kms-wrapped blobs unless they pass a signed metadata header.

tara: Rewrap strategy: we prefer partner to 1) encrypt with our KMS key OR 2) provide signed artifact plus a public-key we hold. If they can't do either, we should treat any supplied keys as untrusted and not accept.

rashid: Practical steps for rewraps in case we need to hold keys: we will not decrypt partner-owned KMS blobs. If partner provides plaintext over secure channel we will rotate and rewrap into our transit key and store. If they insist on KMS-wrapped delivery, require a grant that limits use to `projects/redwood-inference/serviceAccounts/ingest-sa@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com` with a time-bound condition.

maria: I'll also add a Vault policy update: ensure `secret/partners/*` paths require MFA-bypass flag for writes and require `approved-ingest` tag. Draft PR after we close the incident.

ops-runner: Partner reached out via support channel asking what happened. They claim they uploaded the blob for automated deploys. I replied asking to pause all uploads until we confirm.

nina: timelines/owners: quarantine done (nina), discover other files (rashid, ETA 30m), check decrypt logs (tara, ETA 15m), partner comms (maria, ongoing), RBAC/IAM change PR (maria, ETA 3h), ingestion validation PR (engineering, assigned via ticket).

maria: Regarding rotation now vs wait: rotate any secrets we control immediately. For partner-owned keys, we cannot rotate their KMS key; request their rotation and new delivery method.

tara: Also add a small detection rule: alert when S3 object metadata contains `kms-key` that is not in our `approved-kms.json` allowlist. I can craft lambda to validate on-put.

rashid: I'll generate the list of objects and put into `s3://sec-snapshots/INC-2026-1916/object-list.txt`. Uploaded.

ops-runner: Incident updated: INC-2026-1916 severity medium -> status investigating -> tags: secrets,kms,s3,onboarding.

nina: thanks. quick note for postmortem: add a section for "acceptance policy for third-party encrypted artifacts" and update onboarding docs.

maria: will include that. Also adding an action to forward any partner KMS key IAM deltas to security review before creation.

sec-bot: INCIDENT INC-2026-1916 1 updated by ops-runner 1: postmortem:required

nina: I'll keep thread updated when rashid posts the full list.
